en: The Sūtra of the Eight Auspicious Ones, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghabara of Funan during the Liang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
He was together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus, eighty thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and others.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śāriputra:

"From this buddha-world, proceeding toward the east past as many worlds as there are grains of sand in one Ganges River, there is a world named Devajaya. In that land there is a Buddha named Suvyākaraṇaśrī Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently preaching the Dharma."

“Śāriputra! From that buddha-world, proceeding toward the east, past as many worlds as there are grains of sand in two Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Smṛtimatī. In that land there is a Buddha named Samantaprabhāsa Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently dwelling and preaching the Dharma.”

“Śāriputra! To the east of that buddha-world, passing through as many worlds as there are grains of sand in three Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Lovely Play. In that land there is a Buddha named Victorious in Battle Auspiciousness (Saṃgrāmajitaśrī), a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma.”

"Śāriputra! From that world, proceeding toward the east, past as many worlds as there are grains of sand in four Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Sukhaviśuddharāśi. In that land there is a Buddha named Svayambhūdhvajarāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma."

“Śāriputra! From that buddha-world, proceeding toward the east, past worlds as numerous as the sands of five Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Arajodharā. In that land there is a Buddha named Anantaguṇaprabhāsasiri Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently residing and preaching the Dharma.”

“Śāriputra! To the east of that buddha-world, passing through as many worlds as there are grains of sand in six Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Unobstructed Play. In that land there is a Buddha named Unobstructed Karma-Pillar Auspiciousness Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently dwelling and preaching the Dharma.”

“Śāriputra! To the east of that buddha-world, passing through as many worlds as there are grains of sand in seven Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Golden Accumulation. In that land there is a Buddha named Subhūṣitavīrya Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently dwelling and preaching the Dharma.”

“Śāriputra! From that buddha-world, proceeding toward the east past worlds as numerous as the sands of eight Ganges Rivers, there is a world named Beautiful Sound. In that land there is a Buddha named Jewel Lotus Abiding King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently residing and preaching the Dharma.”
“Śāriputra! These eight buddha-fields are all entirely pure; there are no women therein, nor are there the five corruptions. Śāriputra!”

If good sons or good daughters who abide in the Mahāyāna hear the names of these eight Buddhas, uphold them without forgetting, and also explain them to others, it is impossible that they should be reborn in the three miserable realms or the eight difficult conditions.

If there is a woman who hears the names of these eight Buddhas and is able to remember and uphold them, and furthermore explains them to others, it is impossible for her to receive a female body again.

“Śāriputra! If good men or good women who abide in the Mahāyāna hear the names of these eight Buddhas, and having heard them, receive and uphold them and explain them to others, they will always possess supernormal powers in both this life and future lives; they will attain the eloquence of joyful speech, deeply cultivate meditative concentration, and be endowed with dhāraṇīs. Their six sense faculties will be pure, and they will constantly encounter holy beings. They will have no fear of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, non-humans, thieves, water, fire, or poisonous drugs; all terrors will be utterly extinguished. Whether sleeping or waking, they will always be at peace, free from all evil dreams, and will be constantly protected by the various devas.”
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this geya:
“If there are good men, as well as women, who hear the names of these eight buddhas, and remember them, uphold them, and explain them to others, [they shall attain supreme enlightenment].”
Body and mind are always peaceful and secure, free from all terrors.
With mindfulness fixed and never lost, one extinguishes the sins of immeasurable kalpas;
subsequently born among devas and humans, one remains far removed from the evil realms.
The six sense faculties are ever pure; upright and majestic, they possess great dignity.
The eight classes of benevolent deities constantly provide protection throughout the night.
Honored by humans and devas, they receive offerings that bring them joy.
Yakṣas and non-humans, thieves and weapons,
water, fire, poisons, and the like— none of these fears shall exist;
whether sleeping or awake, one will always be peaceful and secure, free from all evil dreams.
Those of sharp faculties and wisdom, who always delight in hearing the True Dharma,
and having heard it, give rise to faith and attain the profound and wondrous Dharma—
such people have no foul odor from their mouths and diligently teach it to others.
Neither the hosts of Māras nor the non-Buddhists shall dare to disturb them.
When women hear the name of the Buddha, remember and uphold it, and speak of it to others,
they will exhaust this female retribution and never receive another birth as a woman thereafter.
Reciting and upholding these names, and explaining them for others,
one shall obtain all the fruits of merit as described above. Therefore,
those who possess wisdom should solely contemplate and uphold them.
"With a single mind harboring joy, you should not give rise to negligence.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the Elder Śāriputra and the other great bhikṣus, as well as the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, and the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Sūtra of the Eight Auspicious Ones (Aṣṭamaṅgalika-sūtra)
